what: Two substitutions, one per half of the change (rule 9). The first half is the guard's sight — a comparison that varies the focus rather than holding it constant; the second half is the layout fix — the crew's caption laying only its name in the first pass. Each mutant is run against a committed state, so putting the mutant back cannot take the change with it.
howMutantsAreRun: python rewrites the one named line in the working copy, dotnet test runs the named filter, then `git checkout -- <file>` puts the line back. The was/became texts are verbatim, including leading spaces.
whyTheTwoAreNotOneChangeCutInHalf: Reverting the whole change would redden the guard and prove only that something was reverted. These two separate the halves: mutant «symptom» keeps the sighted guard and reverts the layout, and the guard fails on the owner's own gesture. Mutant «blindGuard» reverts the layout and *also* blinds the guard, and everything is green. The second is the one this Issue was opened for — it is what «проверка, которая не может увидеть свой дефект» looks like as a number rather than as a claim.
